basics.name: Brett Boggs
basics.label: Co-founder, Datum
basics.summary: Co-founder of Datum, an all-in-one construction management platform, building the product end to end as full-stack engineer: design, frontend, backend, architecture, security, infrastructure, and release. Before that, a decade running physical operations, a car wash chain and a real estate investment company, where the same instinct turned manual intake, correspondence, and reporting into systems that ran without me.

work.name: Datum
work.summary: One system for running a construction company: projects, people, equipment, safety, and money in one place. Full-stack engineer: architecture, security, infrastructure and release. Launched with a beta client in 2025.
highlights: 2,122 HTTP endpoints across 338 backend services
908 tables in Azure SQL, behind 507 tracked migrations
300 screens and 338 shared components in React
132 standard operating procedures, automated end to end
Tenant isolation enforced at the query layer, role based access through Entra ID
ERP adapter framework with a durable writeback queue, normalizing phase codes and cost types
GDPR deletion and data subject export across three previously unconnected identity systems
React Native app through TestFlight, an Outlook add-in, CI/CD into Azure with health checks and uptime monitoring

work.name: Providence Capital
work.summary: Operations for a real estate investment company: the intake-to-close documentation workflow, the correspondence, and the reporting that shows where every file stands.
highlights: Owned intake to close for 200+ active files at once, held to 98% accuracy with Salesforce custom fields, validation rules, and automated routing
Rebuilt correspondence from scratch: 12+ standardized templates with conditional language blocks, cutting revision requests 60% and turnaround from 3 days to 1.5
Pushed on-time file delivery from 82% to 97% in 90 days with real-time status dashboards and automated deadline escalations
Removed 85% of cross-team deadline misses by replacing manual handoffs between legal, finance, and closing with automated status triggers
Built a weekly automated reporting dashboard that freed 6 hours a week and gave leadership its first live view of the pipeline

work.name: Tidal Wave Auto Spa
work.summary: Eight locations and forty-plus people: daily operations, staffing, and the documentation that keeps a region legible.
highlights: Built a centralized records system that cut document retrieval from 30 minutes to under 2
Tracked 150+ concurrent tasks at a 94% on-time completion rate with a priority matrix and automated escalation rules
Standardized incident intake with automated routing, cutting report processing time 45%
Replaced reactive check-ins with a weekly reporting cadence and structured regional visibility

work.name: Tidal Wave Auto Spa
work.summary: One location, run as a business.
highlights: Managed a $2.1M annual budget and built monthly KPI dashboards tracking 15+ metrics for regional leadership
Implemented a customer service tracking system that improved response time 35%
100% compliance audit rating two years running

work.name: Freelance photography
work.summary: Commercial, live music, and product photography.

projects.name: brettboggs.dev
projects.description: This site. Astro, static, hand-built design system, a Blender-rendered scroll film on the front page, and a build that measures and logs itself.

projects.name: Sprout Siege
projects.description: An idle farm game for iOS, built around a simulation core that never touches the screen.

projects.name: CRM intake automation
projects.description: Inherited a manual intake process with a 15% error rate and a 3-day turnaround. Redesigned it end to end with custom fields, validation rules, conditional logic, and automated notifications: 100% accuracy, processing time halved, 500+ files a month with almost no manual touch.

projects.name: Multi-location reporting
projects.description: Twelve hours a month of manual compilation across eight locations, with no live view. An automated dashboard in Google Sheets and Salesforce pulling live data, calculating KPIs, and sending weekly exception reports cut that to two hours, read by 20+ people every week.
